newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-DUNHILL CUP LIKELY TO STAY AT OLD COURSE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUNHILL CUP LIKELY TO STAY AT OLD COURSE.

text.p: The Alfred Dunhill Cup team golf event is likely to stay at St Andrews for another three years despite rumours that this week's championship could be the last, a top official said on Tuesday.

Tournament director Peter German said discussions were underway with the company who have supported the three-man team event throughout its 12-year history to renew their contract for another three years.
"We hope to have the contract in place by the end of this week, or if not, very soon after," German said. "I'm confident it will continue for at least one year and, I hope, for three years."

Reports last year that this week's event, which has attracted world number one Greg Norman, Colin Montgomerie, Nick Price and Ernie Els, could be the last, stemmed from dissatisfaction about the bad weather that has often plagued St Andrews in October.
German dismissed suggestions that the event might be moved away from the Old Course -- the "home of golf".
"It will be at St Andrews if it is held anywhere," he said, adding that next year's date would also be in October because of the Ryder Cup in Spain late in September.
But from 1998, he envisioned a move to late September, he said.

German also disclosed there was a possibility that the Scottish Open and the new Loch Lomond Invitational tournaments could be combined next year and held at the impressive Loch Lomond course in the traditional Scottish Open week in July just before the British Open.
The Scottish Open was held for many years at Gleneagles but was staged in 1995 and 1996 at Carnoustie.

Merging the two events would give the Scottish Open, currently without a venue for 1997, a new home and would also help the Loch Lomond organisers who failed to attract the big-name players they had hoped.
German said he expected an announcement by the end of October.
